title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in July 1986 Grothendieck is axiomatizing 'ateliers' (formerly 'magasins'). An atelier is a structure (A, ⊴, °≪, |∘|) whose elements are geometric 'figures'. On this page he develops the 'supports' (contours) attached to an atelier.

The data: |∘| is a symmetric, irreflexive relation on A, to be read as 'separated' or 'disjoint'.

The page continues the previous one. There is a family Σ_A ⊂ P(A) of 'supports'. It is closed under arbitrary intersections, so intersections give arbitrary Inf. It contains ∅ as least element and the whole set as greatest element.

The implicit construction: put S^⊥ = {x : x|∘|y for all y ∈ S}. Supports are the subsets with S = S^⊥⊥. This is the closure system of the Galois connection (polarity) defined by |∘|.

The complement ∁ is S ↦ S^⊥. It is an inclusion-reversing involution ('anti-involution'). It follows that arbitrary Sups exist: Sup S_i = ∁(∩ ∁S_i), the closure of the union. ∁ exchanges Inf and Sup, and least and greatest elements.

|∘| is extended to supports: S|∘|S' iff x|∘|x' for all x ∈ S and x' ∈ S'. Then S|∘|S' ⟺ S ⊂ ∁S' ⟺ S' ⊂ ∁S, which holds by definition of ⊥. Also S|∘|S' ⟹ S∩S' = ∅, but not conversely.

Next step: given a set of figures F together with Δ, he defines inside Σ_A a subfamily of 'constructible' supports, Σcons_A. The next page says this subfamily is generally stable neither under Sup, Inf nor ∁. An 'axiome des supports' is meant to replace that missing stability. Each figure X will have a support X° = the smallest support containing X, interpreted as the stratum dominating X.

Marginal note, 'Structure d'un Spatios': an order relation and a complement ∁ such that
1° least and greatest elements exist;
2° ∁ is an anti-involution;
3° x∧∁x = ∅ and x∨∁x = the top element.
This is exactly the axiom set of an orthocomplemented poset or ortholattice. Grothendieck is abstracting the lattice of supports into a structure he calls a 'Spatios'.

In short, the page reconstructs the classical fact that an orthogonality space (A, |∘|) yields a complete ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets. He uses it as the 'space of supports' of an atelier.
errors: No mathematical error. The claim S|∘|S' ⟹ S∩S' = ∅ needs irreflexivity: a common x would satisfy x|∘|x. He gives this hypothesis on the previous page.
The page never states explicitly that supports are the biorthogonally closed sets, i.e. how Σ_A is defined from |∘|. The equivalence S|∘|S' ⟺ S ⊂ ∁S' requires ∁S = S^⊥, which is left implicit.

Sup in Σ_A is the closure of the union, not the union. The 'Spatios' complement is orthocomplementation, not Boolean complement, since distributivity generally fails. The text says neither explicitly, though 'l'inverse n'est pas vrai en général' hints at it.

ideas.what: From a symmetric irreflexive relation, take the family of S with S = S^⊥⊥ as 'supports'. It is closed under intersections and carries the complement S ↦ S^⊥.
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality space / polarity; complete ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (polarities, Lattice Theory 1940); Dacey (orthospaces, 1968); Foulis–Randall; Galois connections generally

ideas.what: Extending |∘| to supports, with S|∘|S' ⟺ S ⊂ ∁S' and orthogonality implying disjointness but not conversely.
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality of closed subspaces in an ortholattice

ideas.what: Margin 'Spatios': an abstract structure (order, complement) with bounds, anti-involution, and x∧∁x = 0, x∨∁x = 1.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff–von Neumann 1936 (quantum logic), standard lattice theory

ideas.what: A subfamily of 'constructible' supports generated by figures. It is not closed under lattice operations; an 'axiom of supports' replaces that closure. Each figure's support is the smallest support containing it, read as the dominating stratum.
ideas.modern_name: Constructible sets / stratification within an abstract geometry of figures (cf. o-minimal / tame topology axiomatics)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (closest: o-minimal structures, van den Dries; Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' programme)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's lattice of 'supports' of an atelier, which he abstracts as a 'Spatios', is precisely the ortholattice of an orthogonality space, the basic structure of quantum logic. It is being used here for a geometric/stratification theory of figures. The link between his 1986 'ateliers' axiomatics and orthogonality spaces / ortholattices does not appear to have been noted.
missed.quote: Structure d'un Spatios : a) relation d'ordre b) "relation" ∁ ... 2°) ∁ est une anti-involution 3°) x∧∁x = ∅_E ; x∨∁x = Δ_E
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly of historical interest: it shows how his late axiomatics of geometry (tame topology / 'ateliers') was built. The mathematics itself is classical.

missed.claim: Constructible supports are not closed under Sup, Inf or ∁, and an 'axiom of supports' is to compensate. This combination of an orthocomplemented lattice of supports with a non-closed constructible subfamily is announced but its development is deferred.
missed.quote: permet de définir dans Σ_A une partie, formée des parties constructibles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with o-minimal and tame-geometry axiomatics, but it is not clearly novel.

deep.surprise_reason: The core mathematics, an orthogonality relation giving a complete ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets, is classical lattice theory, apparently rediscovered for the 'ateliers' axiomatics. The only mildly notable point is the unrecognized parallel with quantum-logic structures inside an unpublished geometric axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: First line likely reads 'y jouant donc le rôle des Inf quelconques', not 'jouissant dans la rôle'.
Σ_U should be Σ_A (script A misread as U).
The 'E[?]' greatest element is probably the whole set A, written as E or A.
The superscript over ⟺ in the definition of S|∘|S' looks like 'variante' / '(par déf)'; uncertain.
The marginal word 'Rigolaid(E)' is uncertain; it may be a name of an example structure on E; illegible.
